newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore crime unit probes ex-Merrill banker case.
newsitem.headline: Singapore crime unit probes ex-Merrill banker case.

text.p: Singapore's Commercial Affairs Department (CAD) is looking into the case of a former private banker at Merrill Lynch, a spokeswoman said on Tuesday.
"We can confirm that we have received the reports and that we're looking into the matter," she said.

The CAD, Singapore's white collar crime unit, is expected to examine the details of the case to decide if there was evidence of criminal activity, a legal source said. Earlier, a Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) official said the CAD was investigating the case.
"The CAD is investigating it," he said, in answer to a question at a briefing on the MAS 1996/97 annual report.

U.S. securities house Merrill Lynch has said the former employee, Kevin James Wallace, had "engaged in unauthorised trading, misrepresenting or falsifying private clients' statements and forging client signatures".
It also has said it started civil proceedings in Singapore and Hong Kong against Wallace, and filed a criminal complaint in Singapore.
A lawsuit filed in the Singapore High Court by Merrill against Wallace has been sealed to protect confidential customer accounts.
Merrill has not commented on the amount in question in the case but industry sources and media reports have estimated some US$30 million could be involved.
An industry source described Wallace as "one of the top brokers within Merrill handling huge accounts". Merrill has sought to freeze Wallace's assets internationally and prevent their dissipation.
The whereabouts of Wallace were not known.
Asked earlier at the MAS briefing about regulation of the growing private banking sector in Singapore, the official said it was no different from any other financial activity in Singapore.
As a regulator, it is important to ensure that only reputable institutions and professionals are admitted into the industry, he said.
